It's rare to find your purpose for life, so instead look for your purpose for this season. 

What lights you up right now? What's a good thing to dedicate this season of your life to? Perhaps more importantly, what purpose served you well in your previous season, but you have outgrown?
 
Life is always changing. It's okay to pick a new North Star.

I really wish people would stop saying "distribution". 

It's almost meaningless. It's like saying, the only moat now is a lot of people knowing about you. Well no shit, entrepreneur of the year.

What do you really mean? time and trust in the market? owning a valuable earned media channel? a proprietary paid ads strategy that is printing money?

Learn to say what you mean.

If you just keep saying it without knowing what the fuck you're talking about, you're ngmi.

hits.full_text:
when I was younger, I thought “if you’re worrying, you’re probably not the problem” was a smart and correct move to reassure people who were anxious about causing harm. surely only the thoughtless, indifferent people were the harm-causers! And I’d feel proud of myself anytime I helped someone worry less.

turns out it’s not so simple. in the years since I’ve encountered a lot of people who’d actually cause the harm they were worrying about. Sometimes the worrying did nothing. Sometimes it turns out it was reducing the harm a bit. Sometimes it made the harm worse. Directing someone to worry less may or may not help them worry less, in part depending on your skill as a worry-reducer. Supposed you’re skilled at it. You might reduce worries today. It *might* cause more harm as a consequence. So one oughta investigate the situation more thoroughly before issuing a simplistic correction
hits.hook: Visakan: worrying about causing harm doesn't prove you aren't the problem (~10k)

patterns: Season over life: James Clear's 'purpose for this season' line is the biggest post of the day (~99k). Framing a big question as temporary and smaller is what landed.
Reading slumps are everywhere this week, mostly one-line confessions from small book accounts that pull replies with book suggestions.
Starting over fatigue: several short posts say the restart itself isn't the problem, repeating it is. People reply to these with their own versions.
ADHD posts that land describe the actual scaffolding (blank planners, eat timers, Lego instructions, writing sprints with body doubles) and push back on cute reframes.
Fountain pens: lots of newcomers and messy refills, plus inventive tools like a browser fountain pen simulator from a 100-year-old Japanese pen shop.
Watchlist founder talk is Yongfook again (three posts past 5k) on terminals, AI writing its own prompts, and 'distribution' being a hollow word.

reply_ideas.description: pushing back on calling ADHD a gift, describing a mostly blank planner, fourteen half-finished things on the counter, and a phone timer to remember to eat
reply_ideas.reply_text: I don't think the planner and the phone timer are proof of a gift or proof of failure. They're the stuff you built so the day works, and I'd rather people call it that than dress it up. Which of the fourteen things on the counter would you actually miss if it vanished?

reply_ideas.description: a book account saying she's in a serious reading slump and it's making her sad
reply_ideas.reply_text: I think a slump sometimes gives way to a reread, because there's nothing to decide and the book can't let you down. Is it that nothing sounds good right now, or that you start books and can't stay in them?

reply_ideas.description: Japan's 100-year-old fountain pen shop just released an English version of its free fountain pen simulator
reply_ideas.reply_text: I write with a fountain pen every day, so I'm curious how you got a screen to act like a nib. Did you base the ink flow on one of your own pens?

x_posts.title: Same lessons
x_posts.text:
Two posts on my feed today said nearly the same thing. One person doesn't mind starting over but is tired of learning the same lessons, and another is worn out from starting over when all they want is for something to finally work. I think starting over gets heavy when every restart has to be the big one.

What's the smallest restart you've made that actually held?
x_posts.why: starting-over fatigue posts from small accounts

x_posts.title: Nothing to decide
x_posts.text:
Someone doing Novel November said the writing sprints work for her ADHD because they run on timers and other writers act as body doubles, so there's nothing to decide. I think having nothing to decide is an underrated writing tool.

Do you write better alone or with someone else in the room?
x_posts.why: Novel November ADHD sprint post; concrete ADHD scaffolding outperforming reframes
